## Hook (first 3 seconds)
**On-screen text:** "Your coffee tastes flat because of this."
**Visual:** Hard cut to a blade grinder mid-spin — uneven grounds flying, some powder, some chunks. Lid off, shot from directly above.
**VO:** "This grinder is wrecking your coffee — and it's not the beans."

*Hook archetype: Negative framing + demonstrated outcome. The problem is visible in frame one, muted, from the top.*

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — The problem, named (≈4s)**
*Cut to split screen: blade grounds (left) vs. burr grounds (right).*
On-screen text: "Blade = chaos. Burr = even."
VO: "A blade chops. You get dust and boulders in the same cup."

**Scene 2 — Why it ruins the cup (≈5s)**
*Pour-over close-up: water hitting the uneven bed, draining unevenly.*
On-screen text: "Dust over-extracts. Boulders under-extract."
VO: "The fine bits burn bitter. The big bits stay sour. Same brew, fighting itself."

**Scene 3 — The fix, shown (≈5s)**
*Burr grinder dispensing a uniform, consistent grind into a basket. Satisfying, settled shot.*
On-screen text: "Uniform grind = even extraction."
VO: "A burr grinder cuts every particle the same size. That's consistency you can actually taste."

*Structure: Myth/correction. The payoff lands here, before the ask.*

## CTA
**On-screen text:** "Send this to whoever bought the cheap grinder."
**VO:** "Know someone still grinding with blades? Send them this before their next bag."
**Final frame:** Loop back to the side-by-side — even grounds held in focus.

*One ask, tuned for reshare (the top Shorts/feed signal). No engagement bait.*
